name: ALGERIA

flag.title: Flag of Algeria
flag.note: Green & white with red crescent & star

lead: Algeria is the biggest country in Africa. It could swallow all of western Europe. Most of it is Sahara desert, with dunes and green oases (spots with water). Algiers, the capital, is called "the White City" for its gleaming hilltop houses.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The Sahara covers 90 % of Algeria, the largest hot desert on Earth. Most of it is bare rock and gravel called 'reg', not sandy dunes.
The Ahaggar Mountains rise from the Sahara like a moonscape of ancient volcanic spires. In the Chiffa Gorge, Barbary macaques watch cars go by.
animals: The fennec fox is the world's smallest wild fox. Its huge ears hear beetles walking under the sand. Addax antelope cross the dunes. Sand cats prowl after dark on wide, flat paws.
Barbary macaques live in the Atlas cedar forests. Horned vipers zigzag across desert rock. The rare Saharan cheetah still roams the far south.
culture: Couscous is steamed semolina grains served over lamb and vegetables. On Friday, families eat lunch together, with merguez sausage and honey-soaked almond pastries.
Berber carpets from Ghardaïa are woven by hand with bold diamond shapes. Raï music was born in Oran and spread worldwide. The old casbah in Algiers is a UNESCO maze of white staircases.
history: Berber (Amazigh) people have lived here for 10,000 years. Phoenicians built coastal cities. Romans left Timgad, a whole city still standing in the desert. Later, Ottoman corsairs (pirates) made European kings tremble.
France conquered Algeria in 1830. After an eight-year war of independence, Algeria became free on 5 July 1962. It is the proudest holiday on the calendar.
wows: Algeria is bigger than all of Western Europe combined.
Rock paintings at Tassili n'Ajjer show elephants living where Sahara sand now blows.
Oil and gas make up about 95 % of Algeria's foreign earnings.
Sand buried Timgad's Roman grid for 1,000 years before people found it.
In 1627, Algerian corsairs raided as far north as Iceland.
Algeria has seven UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The fennec fox never needs to drink, because insects and roots give it water.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: Camel humps hold fat, not water. The fat gives a camel energy when food is scarce.
Wind pushes dunes along, grain by grain. Some travel several metres every year.
